whatItIs: QuantumTomography.jl is an open-source project in the visualization and tomography category. It is maintained by BBN-Q and primarily looks like a Julia codebase. This is a package that provides basic routines to perform quantum tomography of finite dimensional systems.

For readers mapping the ecosystem, this resource is useful because it shows how one team approaches visualization and tomography workflows in practice. The repository README emphasizes: This is a package that provides basic routines to perform quantum tomography of finite dimensional systems. Given the estimated means and variances of the observations, tomography proceeds by finding the state, process, or measurements that optimize some figure of merit -- either the likelihood or the χ² statistic...
whoItsFor: People who learn best by seeing state structure, measurement results, or circuit behavior laid out visually.
whatYouCanBuild: Understand how the project helps inspect or reconstruct quantum systems.
Compare visual tooling against more code-heavy workflows.
Use the resource as a bridge between theory, experiments, and debugging.
readmeExcerpt: This is a package that provides basic routines to perform quantum tomography of finite dimensional systems. Given the estimated means and variances of the observations, tomography proceeds by finding the state, process, or measurements that optimize some figure of merit -- either the likelihood or the χ² statistic -- often with the additional constraint the reconstruction be physical (e.g., correspond to a valid quantum mechanical object).
